text:
maria: kicking off a small canary for routing-policy v2 — 5% traffic. want the dashboard guards locked before any ramp. quick sync?

deploy-bot: Canary started: routing-policy v2 (id=canary-2026-03-18-77) -> 5% traffic

jake: what exact signals should guards evaluate? p95, error rate, cost, or something else?

sophie: must-haves: p95, 5xx rate, and 99.9 tail for timeout detection. prefer both relative delta and absolute thresholds.

kai: add kv-cache hit-rate and inference CPU spike alerts. routing changes often shift seq-length mix.

alan: UX ask: traffic-split control with a guard toggle that can auto-rollback. show active guards and last firing reason inline by the slider.

maria: console needs canary vs baseline overlay, a delta band, and an expandable guard panel with per-metric rules.

jake: rules should be composable. example logic: (err_delta > 0.005) AND (p95_canary > max(200ms, p95_baseline*1.25))

sophie: also want an OR-path for high user-impact drops: if success_rate falls > 0.008 -> immediate rollback.

jake: rough rule draft for discussion:
```
name: guard_err_and_latency
conditions:
  - metric: error_rate
    comparator: delta_gt
    value: 0.005
  - metric: p95_latency
    comparator: ratio_gt
    ratio: 1.25
action: rollback
window: 5m
severity: high
```

maria: good. console builders should be pickers (metric, comparator, threshold) with a YAML/JSON preview for power users.

alan: presets would help — "safe", "balanced", "fast-rollout" — show expected rollback frequency (historical) for each.

kai: telemetry: tag every metric by route, model_version, region, customer_tier. drilldowns must link to those slices and allow quick compare.

jake: and attach sample traces to the anomalous bucket. clicking the percentage delta should open a few representative traces.

sophie: where do canary alerts go? we shouldn't flood #incidents. propose #canary-alerts with on-call integration and severity remapping.

maria: agreed. alerts payload should include estimated affected RPS, quick rollback button, and a link to the guard rule that fired.

metrics-bot: Canary snapshot -> p95_baseline=170ms p95_canary=260ms (+53%), error_rate_baseline=0.18% err_canary=0.95% (+0.77%), rps_canary=130

jake: that err delta > 0.7% exceeds our default guard. algorithmic decision: compare canary 5m window vs baseline 1h and optionally vs same-hour-previous-day. reduces diurnal flakiness.

sophie: baseline window config is important. support time-shift comparisons (previous day/week) and a minimum sample size.

maria: decision: start at 5%, hold for 10m, auto-rollback if any guard fires. Alan -> mock guard preset UI by EOD. Jake -> add metric tags + trace link endpoints. Sophie -> formalize severity-to-channel mapping.

alan: done. initial mock at https://redwood.internal/proto/guard-ui-v1 (proto link)

jake: I'll spike metrics tagging and trace-link plumbing, PR to metrics-service tomorrow AM.

sophie: adding a "mute canary" action too (temporarily pause alerts) for noisy infra events but still keep telemetry.

maria: console safety rule: prevent traffic >50% without explicit two-step confirmation and a second approver. also warn if baseline window < 30m.

deploy-bot: Canary canary-2026-03-18-77 rolled back automatically (trigger: error_rate delta > 0.007) by pipeline #deploy-319

maria: nice. schedule a short postmortem in eng-platform tomorrow 11:00 to capture lessons and finalize guard presets. thanks all :thumbsup:
